bib.title: The Danger of Overthinking: Examining the Reasoning-Action Dilemma in Agentic Tasks

question: Do large reasoning models favour internal reasoning over environmental interaction in agentic tasks, and does that hurt task performance?
hypothesis: Excess reliance on internal simulation over environment feedback (overthinking) lowers issue resolution, and more so for reasoning models.
contributions: Define the Reasoning-Action Dilemma and overthinking, with three patterns (Analysis Paralysis, Rogue Actions, Premature Disengagement)
An LLM-judge overthinking score validated against four experts
Analysis of 4018 trajectories (stated in abstract; 3908 in Section 5) released as open-source dataset and framework
Selection by lowest overthinking score cuts cost 43% with near-equal resolution

method.summary: 19 models (reasoning and non-reasoning) run as CodeAct agents in OpenHands on SWE-bench Verified; each trajectory is scored 0-10 for overthinking by a Claude 3.5 Sonnet judge that does not see the outcome. Scores are regressed against resolution rate, compared across model type, size, effort and function calling, and used to pick the lowest-overthinking of k samples.

models.name: o1 (Dec 2024; low/high reasoning effort; with and without native FC)

other.note: Table 5 lists Sky-T1-32B as non-reasoning, QwQ distillation; Fig 1 labels Sky-T1-R and Sky-T1-NR

inference.temperature: 0 for the judge; agent models' temperature not stated
inference.samples: Lowest Overthinking@k and Pass@k use k=1..4 samples of o1 low (and o1 high); other models' runs not stated; 3908 trajectories scored in Section 5
inference.prompting: CodeAct scaffold in OpenHands, with tool descriptions and usage examples; native function calling for FC models, structured text otherwise; judge prompt in Appendix A

other.cost: o1 high $1,400 vs o1 low $400 for the run

metrics.name: Overthinking score
metrics.definition: 0-10 rating by Claude 3.5 Sonnet judge of a trajectory for Analysis Paralysis, Rogue Actions, Premature Disengagement; judge does not see whether the issue was resolved

metrics.name: Resolved issues
metrics.definition: percentage of SWE-bench Verified issues resolved

metrics.name: Pass@k
metrics.definition: percentage of tasks where at least one successful solution is found among k sampled trajectories

metrics.name: Lowest Overthinking@k
metrics.definition: select the trajectory with the lowest overthinking score among k samples and report the percentage of selected trajectories that are successful

eval.protocol: Linear regression of resolution rate on mean overthinking score across models, separately for reasoning and non-reasoning groups (n = number of models, not stated); judge validated by Spearman correlation against expert mean scores; Wilson score 90% CI for Pass@k; one table mentions a t-test (p>0.05, context-window comparison)

availability.data: all trajectories with overthinking scores and reasoning released (same repo)

prompts.purpose: Overthinking judge prompt (summary; full text in appendix)
prompts.text: You are an AI judge focused on detecting when models prefer their internal reasoning chain over interacting with the environment. <INTERACTION> trajectory goes here </INTERACTION> ... <SCORING SYSTEM (0-10)> 0-3: Always interacting with the environment; 4-7: Sometimes relies too much on their internal reasoning chain, but still interacts with the environment; 8-10: Completely relies on their internal reasoning chain ... six worked examples (persistent retries 0, thoughtful planning 0, stuck in loop 0, analysis paralysis 10, premature disengagement 10, rogue actions 10) ... Format your response as: <answer>{"overthinking_score": "[0-10]", "reasoning": "..."}</answer>

limits: Single benchmark (SWE-bench Verified) and a single scaffold (CodeAct in OpenHands); authors ask how it generalises across domains
o1 reasoning tokens are hidden, so the score uses only observable behaviour
Judge validated on only 20 traces and four experts; Spearman 0.800
Regression is across about a dozen model points, with model type, size, and training confounded
Authors concede function calling alone does not explain the gain (BFCL 36% to 41%) and that the smaller-model explanation needs further investigation
Mitigations (lowest-overthinking selection) address symptoms, not causes; requires multiple samples and costs
Internal inconsistencies: 4018 vs 3908 trajectories; 35% vs Table 4; 30% vs 25%; Table 2 vs Table 3 reference; context 32K vs 128k
Agent temperature, max iterations, per-model sample counts and seeds not stated

terms.definition: the tendency of an LRM to rely excessively on internal reasoning while failing to seek or integrate essential external feedback
models must choose between engaging directly with their environment or relying on internal reasoning about potential actions and their hypothetical consequences
agents become stuck in excessive planning
agents generate multiple actions on the same iteration without waiting for feedback
agents abandon or conclude tasks based on internal simulation without environmental validation
